candidates.source_name: Narodna banka Srbije — Propisi / Odluke (banking regulation and supervisory decisions)
candidates.why_relevant: Serbia is the largest regional home/host jurisdiction adjacent to Montenegro; Serbian-owned or Serbia-domiciled groups (e.g. AIK/Agri Europe cluster, Serbian bidders for Montenegrin banks) are supervised here. NBS regulatory changes on payments, IPS instant payments, capital and consumer protection are frequently copied or anticipated by CBCG, and Serbian bidders for Montenegrin bank stakes require NBS clearance before/alongside CBCG approval.
candidates.source_subtype: national central bank / supervisor regulation portal
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled HTML crawl of the propisi/odluke listing pages plus RSS/news page; diff on document lists; store PDFs of odluke
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search (sr) on regulator + subsidiary terms
queries_used: Narodna banka Srbije odluka banka Crna Gora podružnica regulativa

candidates.source_name: Hrvatska narodna banka (HNB) — Supervizija / Regulativa
candidates.why_relevant: Croatia is the euro-area/SSM member closest to Montenegro linguistically and commercially; HNB's transposition of EU banking and payments law (Zakon o platnom prometu, CRR/CRD, PSD2/PSD3 prep) is a leading indicator of what Montenegro will adopt during EU accession alignment. Croatian-language texts are directly readable by Montenegrin practitioners and often reused in CBCG drafting.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl regulations and payment-system licensing pages; monitor 'Novosti'/press releases; capture Narodne novine references cited
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search (hr) for supervision + payment regulation
queries_used: Hrvatska narodna banka HNB odluke supervizija objave regulativa platni promet

candidates.source_name: Agencija za bankarstvo Federacije BiH (FBA)
candidates.why_relevant: FBA publishes laws, subordinate regulations, reporting frameworks and a 'regulations in preparation' section — a rare pre-consultation window. Several groups present in Montenegro (ASA/ASA-Addiko cluster, Intesa, UniCredit, ProCredit, Sparkasse) also hold FBiH subsidiaries, so FBA supervisory actions reveal group-level pressure before it surfaces in Podgorica.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl 'Regulativa' and 'Propisi u pripremi' listings on a weekly diff; archive PDFs
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search (bs/sr) for entity banking agencies
queries_used: Centralna banka Bosne i Hercegovine Agencija za bankarstvo FBiH RS propisi banke

candidates.source_name: Agencija za bankarstvo Republike Srpske (ABRS)
candidates.why_relevant: The second BiH entity supervisor; a signatory of the EBA Memorandum of Cooperation alongside Montenegro. Its regulation set and enforcement actions are a comparator for CBCG and cover banks with cross-border exposure to Montenegro.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Weekly crawl of regulation/news sections; URL inferred from agency name — verify base path in the liveness pass
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from BiH supervisory architecture (CBBH coordinates the two entity agencies)
queries_used: Centralna banka Bosne i Hercegovine Agencija za bankarstvo FBiH RS propisi banke

candidates.source_name: Centralna banka Bosne i Hercegovine (CBBH)
candidates.why_relevant: CBBH coordinates the two entity banking agencies and runs BiH payment systems; useful for regional payment-infrastructure and SEPA-alignment signals and for cross-border financial-stability reporting that includes Montenegro comparators.

candidates.source_name: NLB Group — Investor Relations / Investor News
candidates.why_relevant: NLB is the parent of NLB Banka Podgorica and the largest SEE-headquartered group. Its regulated disclosures carry group capital requirements (SREP), MREL, resolution planning and M&A that bind the Montenegrin subsidiary — including the 2026 voluntary public takeover offer for Addiko Bank AG, which would reshape ownership across the Western Balkans. Group disclosure typically precedes any CBCG announcement.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll investor-news and press-release index pages daily; extract dated items; cross-link to SEOnet filings

candidates.why_relevant: Statutory filing venue where NLB d.d. publishes inside information and general-meeting convocations. Filing here is the legally authoritative, earliest timestamp for group decisions that flow down to NLB Banka Podgorica.

candidates.source_name: European Banking Authority (EBA) — cooperation with South-Eastern European supervisors
candidates.why_relevant: The EBA Memorandum of Cooperation, signed under the Vienna Initiative, formally binds Montenegro's CBCG into EU supervisory-college practice with BiH, RS, North Macedonia, Serbia and Albania. EBA guidelines and Q&As adopted at EU level are the template CBCG follows, usually with a lag — a strong forward indicator of Montenegrin rulemaking.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Subscribe to EBA consultations and guidelines feeds; filter for third-country/enlargement and payments items

candidates.source_name: Vienna Initiative (European Bank Coordination Initiative)
candidates.why_relevant: The standing coordination forum between CEE/SEE home and host supervisors and the cross-border banking groups that own most Montenegrin banks. Its working-group papers name supervisory-college and resolution-cooperation issues years before they appear in national rulebooks, and its deleveraging monitors quantify parent-to-subsidiary funding pressure into Montenegro.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated, structured register of cross-border 'group decision -> Montenegrin subsidiary effect' was found in any language. Group-level facts must be reconstructed by joining parent-issuer regulated filings (SEOnet, BET, Vienna/Wiener Boerse) with CBCG's own licence register.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches in sr and en returned parent-group IR pages and law-firm guides, but no consolidated regional register linking group decisions to Montenegrin subsidiaries.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Means the workstream needs a constructed join, not a single feed; increases collection cost and makes the parent-issuer feeds higher priority.

negative_findings.description: The Serbian-language seed query combining parent-bank/subsidiary terms with Montenegro ('matična banka grupa odluka podružnica Crna Gora regulativa') returned only generic NBS statutory pages and no Montenegro-specific regional regulatory items.
negative_findings.result_summary: sr-language search surfaced the Zakon o Narodnoj banci Srbije and NBS institutional pages only; nothing on cross-border subsidiary decisions.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests the local-language vocabulary needs refinement toward deal/consent wording ('saglasnost za sticanje kvalifikovanog učešća', 'prenos vlasništva nad bankom') rather than corporate-structure wording; a naive sr query set will under-retrieve.

negative_findings.description: URLs for ABRS (abrs.ba), Udruženje banaka Srbije (ubs-asb.com), CBBH (cbbh.ba), Addiko IR and EPC were inferred from institutional names and secondary references rather than fetched during this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Not fetched in this run; recorded with reduced confidence scores.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These must be confirmed by the deterministic liveness pass before being promoted; a non-200 on first try should be treated as a hypothesis, not a dead source.

negative_findings.description: SeeNews and Paragraf Lex are commercial and at least partly subscription-gated; Bloomberg Adria and eKapija use registration walls on some items.
negative_findings.result_summary: Full-text access to the strongest regional cross-border reporting is likely licensed rather than open.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Budget/licensing decision is required if the workstream depends on early cross-border M&A and supervisory-action reporting; otherwise coverage is headline-only.

coverage_gaps.description: Italian and Austrian parent groups with Montenegrin or adjacent exposure (Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit, Erste Group, Addiko, Sparkasse) were not individually source-mapped in this pass beyond the SSM/SRB umbrella and the Addiko takeover thread.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a per-parent issuer feed list (Borsa Italiana, Wiener Boerse, group IR pages, home-supervisor registers) keyed to the CBCG list of licensed banks and their ultimate owners.

coverage_gaps.description: No Albanian- or Macedonian-language sources were covered, although North Macedonia and Albania joined SEPA on the same track as Montenegro and share the same EU alignment timetable.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a short sq/mk glossary and cover Banka e Shqipërisë and Narodna banka RSM as regional comparators for the same reform milestones.

coverage_gaps.description: Official gazettes as primary legal-effect sources were only reached indirectly (via Paragraf and HNB references to Narodne novine / Službeni glasnik).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add direct gazette portals (Službeni glasnik RS, Narodne novine HR, Službeni glasnik BiH) as authoritative-text and effective-date sources for the regional comparator layer.

coverage_gaps.description: Consultation/public-hearing mechanics for the regional regulators (how and where 'javna rasprava' drafts are posted, and with what comment deadlines) were not resolved to specific landing pages.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate and register the javna-rasprava/consultation subpages of NBS, HNB, FBA and ABRS so comment-window deadlines can be tracked as structured events.

coverage_gaps.description: Regional card-scheme, ATM/POS-acquiring and payment-infrastructure operators (regional processors, ACH/instant-payment operators such as Serbia's IPS, Croatia's NKS) were not covered as spillover sources.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Map regional payment-infrastructure operators whose scheme rules and mandates reach Montenegrin acquirers and issuers via parent-group contracts.

brief: Montenegro's regulatory reality is largely written elsewhere: roughly three quarters of banking assets sit with foreign-controlled banks, so the earliest, most binding signals appear in parent-group regulated filings (NLB via SEOnet, OTP via Budapest, Addiko via Vienna) and in supranational layers — ECB/SSM and SRB for euro-area parents, EBA and the Vienna Initiative for the formal home-host cooperation framework that already names CBCG. A second, highly readable layer is the Serbian, Croatian and Bosnian regulators (NBS, HNB, FBA, ABRS), whose rulebooks and consultation drafts function as templates and lead indicators for CBCG's EU-alignment work, with Croatian texts especially close to what Montenegro adopts. The cross-border payments layer — European Commission DG NEAR, the European Payments Council rulebooks and the World Bank's Western Balkans payments programme — carries hard dates that landed on Montenegrin banks through the 2024-2025 SEPA accession. The main weaknesses are that no consolidated group-to-subsidiary register exists (the join must be built), that the sharpest regional M&A and supervisory reporting sits behind SeeNews/Paragraf paywalls, and that the specific consultation ('javna rasprava') landing pages for the regional regulators still need to be pinned down.
